Assumptions and limitations

Page budget: 1 page

[TEAM: Introduce the table; add anything specific to your judgement. Target length: 1 page.]

Data

Assumption Why it matters Mitigation
History is representative of the future Models fitted on 2004–2022 may miss new regimes Stress tests, EVT and a locked out-of-sample test period
One frozen snapshot (to 2026-10-26) Numbers change with new data Hashed manifest; refresh is explicit and logged
ETF prices proxy the investable portfolio Tracking error and fees are inside the ETF prices Expense ratios are not deducted twice
FRED keeps only 3 years of the ICE high-yield spread Credit stress needs long history Moody's Baa–Treasury spread (BAA10Y) used instead

Models

Assumption Why it matters Mitigation
Volatility is time-varying Unconditional models lag in crises GARCH-FHS and conditional EVT, backtested
GARCH parameters are uncertain Recent fits sit near the persistence boundary (α + β ≈ 1), which inflates multi-day forecasts Disclosed; 10-day figures shown with historical and √h comparisons
EVT rests on few extreme points Wide confidence intervals at 99.9% Profile and bootstrap intervals; two threshold rules
Few tail observations to validate 99% VaR About 10 exceptions expected in 4 years; low test power Confidence intervals, power figures and 95% results
Normal model shown as a benchmark only It understates fat tails Never used for decisions
Exceptions still cluster in 2008–2018 Independence is rejected on that period Disclosed; validation 2019–2022 used for selection

Portfolio

Assumption Why it matters Mitigation
Expected returns are estimates (CAPM, MRP 5%) Optimisers are sensitive to μ Ledoit-Wolf Σ, CAPM prior, bootstrap stability
Costs approximated at 5 bps per side No market impact in a crisis Quarterly rebalancing keeps turnover low
Fully invested (cash only as a sensitivity) No liquidity buffer by default T-bill sleeve toggle

Stress

Assumption Why it matters Mitigation
Historical paths may not repeat The next crisis may differ Factor-driven hypothetical and reverse stress
Factor betas are unstable across regimes Scenario impacts are estimates Full-sample and stress-sample betas, SE bands
The hypothetical scenario is one of many Shock sizes and horizon are judgement Anchored on historical extremes; horizon and credit measure to be fixed before the freeze

Decision

Assumption Why it matters Mitigation
Results are provisional until the methodology freeze Champion and ML adoption need the final test Freeze checklist in doc/decisions
Amended limits need client approval The minimum relaxation is a proposal, not a decision Explicit investment-committee approval required
USD base while spending is in LKR FX risk is outside the model Disclosed; LKR scenario as an extension
No derivatives, margin, ESG or tax modelling Out of scope for the universe Stated in the IPS

# AI Disclosure (brief §8.7)

**Status:** draft; the team completes the reviewer names and confirms every statement before submission.

| Item | Disclosure |
|---|---|
| AI tool(s) used | Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code, for implementation support. No other AI tool has been used so far; the team adds any it uses. MiroFish (multi-agent simulator) has **not** been run; Steps 19–20 are optional and gated. |
| Purpose | Implementing modules to the team's written specification (`doc/steps/`); test scaffolding; the Streamlit layout; drafting of documentation, the memo template and the tear-sheet generator; debugging. |
| Human validation | Each module is reviewed and signed off by a named team member (`doc/ai_log.md`). Correctness is checked with closed-form, simulation-recovery, textbook and leakage tests (pytest, 178 tests); results are cross-checked with independent libraries (scipy, statsmodels, arch) and against market facts (for example SPY −54.8% in the GFC window, AGG −15.0% in the 2022 window). |
| Decisions made by the team | The IPS limits and their calibration, the champion-model rule, the stress-scenario assumptions, the verdict logic (`doc/decisions/`), and the final recommendation and its wording. The rule engine and the memo template only assemble evidence; every judgement in the memo is written by the team. |
| Material AI-generated components | Code implementations of the data pipeline, risk models, backtests, stress tests, decision engine, ML challengers and dashboard were AI-assisted. Interpretation and the recommendation are the team's. |

The running log of AI-assisted work, with reviewer and changes after review, is in [`doc/ai_log.md`](doc/ai_log.md).
